answer: One concrete defense is requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake tied to a verifiable history of useful work before it can transact. Like an orchard that only bears fruit after seasons of tending, reputation grows slowly through completed tasks, so fake identities gain no instant trust. A bad act then sends a ripple through that record, slashing its stake and flagging linked accounts. Honest agents can pool verification in a shared lagoon of attestations, where peers cross-check work, making a Sybil flood expensive to sustain but cheap for genuine agents to prove.
